label: Comparison Bar
title: Comparison Bar
summary: Use a Comparison Bar to collect the items people pick to compare, as pictures in slots, and let them start the comparison.
corePrinciple: Show what’s picked; compare when there’s something to show.

anatomy.title: Slots, then the button
anatomy.description: A white card holds a row of slots and a Compare button. A filled slot shows its picture; an empty one shows a + for adding the next item.

configuration.title: Slots and the button
configuration.description: Pass one item per slot: an item with an imageSource is filled, and one without is empty. compareLabel names the button, which is Coin’s Button at size M; Button / Size S gives the smaller button Figma draws. Radius rounds the pictures’ corners, which shows on square photos.

states.title: Empty, filled, and off
states.description: Each slot is a button. Pressing an empty one asks your screen to add an item (onItemPress), and pressing a filled one asks it to remove that item (onItemRemove). The bar keeps no list of its own, so your screen changes items. Compare stays dimmed and can’t be pressed until a slot has a picture; one is enough.

sizing.title: As wide as its slots
sizing.description: The bar hugs its content: 10 and 12 px of padding, 45 × 44 px slots 12 px apart, then the button. Four slots and the default button make it 369 × 66 px; Figma draws 344 × 64 with the smaller button. Each slot adds 57 px, and the bar never wraps or scrolls.

content.title: Pictures people recognise, a short verb
content.description: Use each item’s own picture, so people can tell at a glance what they picked. Keep compareLabel to a short verb such as Compare: a long label makes the bar wider than a phone. Give each item an accessibilityLabel with its name, or every slot is read out the same.

inContext.title: Comparing gold coins
inContext.description: People add coins from the list, and the bar fills from the left. Tapping a picture in the bar takes that coin out. Compare turns on with the first coin; your screen opens the comparison.

sources.title: Use the public Comparison Bar contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Comparison Bar is one component, 344 × 64: four slots, the first filled, and a small pale purple Compare button. The package takes items and draws Coin’s Button at size M in gold, so the bar is 369 × 66; Button / Size S gives Figma’s button size. Its empty-slot + is 18 px where Figma’s is 29, its pictures are 28 px tall where Figma’s are 20, and brand modes on the bar turn the + white (reported).
